# Page 2^page=2
©Idaho State University, 2020 SCOPE AND CONTENT NOTE The Charlton Laird collection includes research files concerning Idaho history that appear to have been class assignments given by Dr. Laird. The research files include oral histories performed by Laird’s students with some early inhabitants and long-time residents of Idaho, providing unique insight into small town and rural pioneer life in the state. Additionally, the collection contains some original correspondence concerning Idaho history, as well as the aborted attempt to start a history periodical entitled, Idaho Historical Quarterly. ARRANGEMENT The Laird collection maintains its original order.

# Page 3^page=3
©Idaho State University, 2020 BIOGRAPHICAL NOTE Charlton Laird was born March 16, 1901 in Nashua, Iowa, the son of John Grant, a businessman, and Elizabeth Richardson Laird. He would later state that his father was an invalid most of the time, and Laird had to put himself through college. Laird emerged from the University of Iowa with a B. A. in 1925 and an M. A. in 1927. His first marriage ended in tragedy when his wife, Floy Davis, died by suicide. Laird’s interest in writing drove his education and his career. Originally trained as a journalist, Laird switched to English, a field in which he received a Ph.D. from Stanford and went on to teach at universities as diverse as Drake University, the University of Idaho Southern Branch, Purdue University, and the University of Nevada, Reno. Laird was employed as an instructor and then assistant professor in the English Department at the University of Idaho Southern Branch (UISB) in Pocatello, Idaho from 1932 until 1942. While on staff at UISB, Laird was responsible for helping create an historical museum on campus and developed an interest in local history. Extensive plans were made for publishing a periodical, the Idaho Historical Quarterly, devoted to Idaho history; however, it never came to fruition. The majority of Laird’s career was spent at the University of Nevada, Reno, joining the staff there in 1943. He was widely published in his area of expertise with numerous scholarly monographs on language, several novels, and many other publications to his credit, including Webster’s New World Thesaurus. Laird was married to Helene P. Gent on June 2, 1945; together they had one child, Nancy (Mrs. Robert Harms). A scholar in her own right, Helene Laird co- wrote at least one volume with her husband. Helene predeceased Charlton in 1979; Laird retired in 1968, but remained affiliated with the University and lived in the Reno area until his death May 14, 1984.
